design:
## Design tests

The refined visuals and the new placement rules were then read blind in six whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v017.md`), the photographer, the one template the v0.16 gate failed, put in three of them, each time with someone to photograph. The camera read as a camera in all three ("holds a camera up to his eye"; no reader said binoculars), the goat as a goat by its horns in all three, the white dog as a dog, the box under the sprinkler as soaked ("is dripping and sits in a puddle, so it is getting soaked"), and the wheelbarrow as standing at rest. No reader saw water coming out of the box, feet on a bench, a pram heading into anyone, a bird on the slide or a thing cut off by the picture's edge.

Two remarks there led to changes before the set was built: a lamp post "almost in front of the lens" (the photographer now needs a clear line to whoever he photographs), and the box's darker wet patches, taken for wood grain or straw (they were dropped, leaving the drips, the run-off and the puddle).
intro: The photographer, the one template that failed the v0.16 gate, passes the fourteenth screen: read as taking a photo in all three of its pictures, each time with someone in front of the lens, and no reader said binoculars. For the third screen running no item was misread, set or probes, and 744 of 748 scored items had full marks; every inference and every contradiction in all 65 pictures was read in full. The set scored 0.995 over all items (0.996 in v0.16), its inferences 1.00 for the first time, with 1.3 unintended oddities per picture (1.1). 63 of 64 templates pass the gate; the one that falls short, the waver, lost half a point in the tier-4 park, where a small girl's raised hand met the dark outline of the hedge line behind her and read as "a string she is holding ... or just a wave".
screen: Across all 65 pictures only 4 of 748 scored items fell short of full marks (3 of 746 in v0.16) and none was misread: three pictures whose readers named the sun but not the clouds, and the waver in the tier-4 park. Unintended oddities rose from 23 to 27 in the set and fell from 37 to 35 in the probes. None of the v0.16 oddities came back as reported then: no water seems to come out of the soaked box, no bird sits on the slide, no pram heads into anyone, no feet stand on a bench, no wheelbarrow looks tipped, and the goat and the white dog were read as what they are. What the readers noticed instead: two figures of different events drawn into each other in a garden; a dark-haired woman in profile whose hair hides her face ("no visible face"); a few sizes off for their depth; a rubbish bin 6 px inside the frame read as "partly cut off"; and, again, goats "unusual to see in a back garden".
redrawn: The photographer passes at 1.00 over three pictures, each with someone to photograph. The visuals refined for the v0.16 oddities read with full marks wherever they were screened: the soaked box ("water is running down its side", "standing in a puddle"), the goat with its darker horns, the white dog with floppy ears reading its newspaper, the wheelbarrows at rest, the railing birds clear of the slide and the pram's deeper lane.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (53 in three, 7 in four, 1 in five, 3 in six). One fails, on a single hedge in the set and no misread: the waver (0.83), read in full in its two other pictures and in all its pictures in v0.15 and v0.16. The v0.18 fix: the waving hand and its motion lines kept clear of the backdrop's outlines, and no waver at the far back.
